claims.text: The starting material is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Cryo-rolling followed by annealing can overcome limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness.
Cryo-rolling and annealing is the proposed single intervention.
The applicable tensile testing or operating condition is room temperature.
Cryo-rolling and annealing creates a novel hierarchical microstructure.
The resulting fine lamellar regions contain FCC lamellae filled with ultrafine FCC grains and B2 lamellae.
The resulting coarse non-lamellar regions contain ultrafine FCC grains, a few coarse recrystallized FCC grains, and relatively coarse unrecrystallized B2 phase.
Cryo-rolling and annealing increases strength relative to the as-cast material.
Cryo-rolling and annealing increases tensile ductility relative to the as-cast material.
The untreated baseline is the as-cast material.
The exact mechanism of the cryo-rolling and annealing process is not fully understood.
Evidence for the effectiveness of cryo-rolling and annealing is based on a limited number of studies.
The intervention may not generalize to all eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing the mechanical properties of cryo-rolled and annealed material against those of as-cast material.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator is stated as the same hierarchical dual-phase lamellar-colony structure already present initially, while the mechanism says the intervention creates a novel hierarchy that also includes coarse non-lamellar regions. The before/after structural distinction is therefore internally ambiguous.
